title: First in, first out; biggest first
description:
Two container adaptors with very different orders.

- `std::queue` hands things back in the order they arrived. Write `std::vector<std::string> serveAll(std::queue<std::string> line)` that removes everyone from the queue and returns their names in the order served.
- `std::priority_queue` always hands back the **largest** element next. Write `std::vector<int> largestFirst(const std::vector<int>& values)` that pushes every value into a priority queue and then pops them all.

Both adaptors have `push`, `pop` (which returns nothing) and `empty`; a queue reads its next element with `front()`, a priority queue with `top()`.
hints: Both functions are the same loop: while the adaptor is not empty, read the next element (`front()` for a queue, `top()` for a priority queue), add it to the result, then `pop()`.
`serveAll` takes the queue by value, so emptying it does not touch the caller's queue.
unitTests:
TEST("a queue serves in arrival order") { std::queue<std::string> q; q.push("Ann"); q.push("Bo"); q.push("Cy"); CHECK_EQ(serveAll(q), (std::vector<std::string>{ "Ann", "Bo", "Cy" })); CHECK(serveAll({}).empty()); }
TEST("a priority queue serves the largest first") { CHECK_EQ(largestFirst({ 3, 9, 1, 9, 4 }), (std::vector<int>{ 9, 9, 4, 3, 1 })); CHECK(largestFirst({}).empty()); }
